summary: Root cause identified with high confidence (0.78): config change cfg-2207, applied by infra-automation at 2026-03-10T09:52Z, reduced portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 via the "cost-optimisation profile small". Within ~4 minutes the HikariPool pegged at exactly total=5/active=5/idle=0 with waiting queues of 45-57 and 3000ms JDBC acquisition timeouts, portfolio-service began failing on /v1/portfolio/holdings, and the api-gateway — whose CPU stayed flat at ~40-46% — returned upstream-timeout 504s for that route. The suspected gateway envoy 1.29->1.30 / HTTP-2 upgrade (dep-5220, 08:00Z) precedes onset by ~2h with no intervening event and its known precedent (HIST-116) presents as "upstream resets", a signature absent from today's logs. The fix is to revert/raise db.pool.max_size; all changes remain live as of 11:59Z, so the incident is likely ongoing.

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service HikariPool shrunk to 5 by cost-optimisation config, pool pegs and 504s propagate to gateway
ranked_hypotheses.statement: On 2026-03-10T09:52Z infra-automation applied cfg-2207, reducing portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 ('cost-optimisation profile small'). Under normal concurrent holdings traffic the 5-slot HikariPool saturates within ~1 minute; requests block for the 3000ms acquisition timeout, the pool pins at exactly 5 in-use (idle=0, waiting up to 57), and portfolio-service returns errors/slow responses. The api-gateway's upstream calls to portfolio-service then exceed their timeout, producing the 504 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings' pattern and the gateway p99 spike. The gateway, and everything else upstream, is a victim.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2207 applied at 09:52Z reduces portfolio-service Datasource pool max_size 50 -> 5
Within ~1-4 minutes the 5-slot pool is fully occupied and new requests cannot acquire a JDBC connection (3000ms acquisition timeout; total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting 45-57)
In-use connections pin at exactly 5.0 from the 09:56Z bucket onward, replacing a ~12-connection baseline, i.e. the cap is pegged
portfolio-service latency p99 jumps (09:45Z bucket avg ~2080ms / max 4546ms) and errors begin at 09:53:19Z

api-gateway calls to portfolio-service wait on the saturated upstream and time out: 252 WARNs of exactly 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings', first at 09:53:53Z; gateway p99 200ms -> ~1.8-4.3s from the 09:50Z bucket
Users see the portfolio page spinning / timing out (SEV-2 report at 10:05Z)

assumptions: The 'small' cost-optimisation profile was applied ahead of or unaware of portfolio-service's real concurrency, so 5 connections is far below what holdings traffic needs (F1 notes no canary/percentage field; the sizing rationale is not in the record)

Pool exhaustion here is occupancy/latency caused by too few slots, not a leaked connection or a slow query holding slots — the DB-layer gaps mean we cannot distinguish, but the abrupt 50->5 step with a matching prior incident makes sizing-by-config the simplest reading
Requests observed at 09:53-09:56Z were representative steady load, i.e. no separate traffic surge was needed to fill 5 slots

ranked_hypotheses.title: api-gateway dep-5220 (envoy 1.29->1.30, HTTP/2 to upstreams) introduced upstream-wait timeouts on the portfolio route
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Reporter's suspicion. dep-5220 at 08:00Z upgraded the gateway envoy filter chain and switched upstream protocol to h2 for portfolio-service and order-service. A defect in that change (HTTP/2 stream/keepalive handling, connection reuse, partial rollout) causes gateway->portfolio connections to stall rather than reset, so gateway requests wait until timeout, producing 504 'upstream timeout portfolio-service' and the p99 spike without any gateway-internal CPU pressure.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5220 deploys api-gateway v9.3.0 at 08:00Z: envoy 1.29->1.30, upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service
A defect or misconfiguration in the new HTTP/2 upstream path causes stalls/timeouts specifically on the portfolio route
Gateway p99 rises from ~200ms baseline to 1.85s (09:50Z) and ~4.3s sustained (09:55Z+); 504 upstream-timeout WARNs dominate the window

assumptions: The 08:00Z change could have a delayed effect ~1h50m later (e.g. only manifesting once connections were recycled or traffic pattern shifted) — no mechanism for this is evidenced
The observed 'upstream timeout' rather than 'upstream reset' text is still compatible with this specific envoy bug, contrary to the HIST-116 precedent

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared ledger-db (or redis-cache) degraded, backpressuring portfolio-service's pool and hence the gateway
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A fault in a shared multi-tenant datastore on the portfolio path — ledger-db (shared by portfolio-service, order-service, payment-service) or redis-cache (shared by auth-service, portfolio-service, market-data-service) — makes queries slow or connections hang, so portfolio-service's JDBC pool is filled by stuck operations. The pool saturation observed in portfolio-service would then be a symptom of the shared-store fault, not of the pool-size config; the gateway is two hops removed.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db / redis-cache are shared:true components on the portfolio path (and shared with order-service, payment-service, auth-service)
One of these shared stores degrades (slow queries, lock contention, refusal or latency), causing portfolio-service's in-flight DB operations to hold connections
portfolio-service's HikariPool fills (total=5, active=5, idle=0) and acquisition times out at 3000ms with waiting counts 45-57
gateway upstream calls to portfolio-service time out -> 504s, p99 spike

assumptions: A shared-store degradation occurred at ~09:52-09:55Z with no recorded change (possible per the gaps: no DB/cache telemetry was queried and un-recorded/slow-burn changes cannot be excluded)
Pool saturation is caused by long-held connections (slow DB) rather than by the cap itself — but F11 shows exact pegging at the *new* cap of 5, which a pure DB slowdown would not produce

ranked_hypotheses.title: Traffic surge / capacity saturation filled portfolio-service's pool with no faulty change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A genuine rise in portfolio-page traffic (or heavy holdings payloads) at ~09:50Z exceeded provisioned DB pool capacity, filling the HikariPool and producing gateway upstream timeouts. No component is misconfigured; capacity is simply insufficient for the load.

causal_chain.claim: Concurrent DB demand exceeds available pool slots, so acquisitions queue and time out
portfolio-service slows -> gateway upstream timeouts -> 504s and p99 spike

assumptions: Such a surge existed and was large enough to saturate a pool that had ~12 average in-use connections against a prior max of 50 — i.e. roughly a 4x+ jump in concurrent demand
Gateway CPU stayed flat (~40-46%) because the load is upstream-wait, not gateway-handled (F12)

facts.statement: A full cross-service change inventory for 2026-03-10 shows exactly one deployment — dep-5220 (api-gateway v9.3.0, 08:00:00Z, envoy 1.29->1.30, upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service, status live, rolled_back_at null) — and two config changes: cfg-2199 (order-service log.sampling_rate, logging only) and cfg-2207 (portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5 at 09:52:00Z by infra-automation, 'Apply cost-optimisation profile "small" to service datasource').

portfolio-service's HikariPool is fully saturated: 503 of 505 in-window log matches are ERROR, split between 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' (270) and 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=...)' (233), with waiting counts of 57, 53, 45.
portfolio-service db_pool_in_use drops to and pins at exactly 5.0 (max=5) from the 09:56Z bucket through 11:56Z, down from a ~12-connection baseline (avg 11.97-12.23, max up to 13.3).

portfolio-service's own p99 15-min bucket jumps from ~181ms (09:30Z) to avg 2079.79 / max 4546.3 at the 09:45Z bucket, and its first ERROR log is 09:53:19Z ('GET /v1/portfolio/holdings failed: could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms').
api-gateway latency_p99_ms jumped from a ~200ms baseline (09:00-09:45Z) to a 5-minute bucket avg of 1849.99ms / max 4418.76ms at 09:50Z, then sustained ~4300ms avg from 09:55Z onward.

The earliest and only gateway WARN signature is an upstream timeout: 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v<n>/portfolio/holdings' with count 252 and first_seen 09:53:53Z — upstream-timeout, not client-timeout or upstream-reset.

The portfolio request path is api-gateway -> portfolio-service -> ledger-db (db), with portfolio-service also calling market-data-service (http) and redis-cache (cache); ledger-db and redis-cache are shared multi-tenant datastores also used by order-service/payment-service and auth-service/market-data-service respectively.

HIST-115 (2025-09-25, order-service) documents the same class of failure as a config change: symptoms ['connection is not available','request timed out','pool exhausted'], root cause 'Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', resolution 'Reverted config; added validation'; the symptom-string query matched it at score 6.

HIST-116 (2025-12-18, api-gateway) documents an envoy upgrade HTTP/2 failure mode but with a different signature — '504 at gateway','upstream resets','timeouts', root cause 'Envoy upgrade changed HTTP/2 max concurrent streams default' — and today's logs show pool-acquisition timeouts rather than upstream resets.

HIST-102 (2025-09-02) shows the same user-visible symptoms (portfolio page timeouts, 504 at gateway) from a different root cause: unplanned ledger-db primary failover with 6 minutes of refused connections (infrastructure_failure).

assumptions: The 'small' cost-optimisation profile was applied without regard to portfolio-service's real concurrency, so 5 connections is far below what holdings traffic needs; the sizing rationale is not recorded (F1 notes no canary/percentage field).

Pool exhaustion is occupancy/latency caused by too few slots rather than a leaked connection or a slow query holding slots — DB-layer telemetry was not queried, so these cannot be separated, but the abrupt 50->5 step plus the HIST-115 precedent make sizing-by-config the simplest reading.
Requests observed at 09:53-09:56Z were representative steady load; no separate traffic surge was required to fill 5 slots.

The 09:45Z portfolio-service p99 bucket is coarse (1-15 min granularity), so a small amount of pre-change rise may be present, and strict ordering between cfg-2207 and the gateway p99 onset depends on bucket boundaries.
The gateway and everything upstream of portfolio-service are victims of the downstream pool saturation rather than independent contributors.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately revert cfg-2207: restore portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 5 back to 50 (roll back the 'cost-optimisation profile "small"' application on the service datasource).
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2207 is the only change on the portfolio path and immediately precedes onset; HIST-115 shows the identical pool-exhaustion signature resolved by reverting the pool-size config (F15). This is the direct addressable cause of the pinned pool (F10, F11).

recommended_actions.action: Hold off on rolling back dep-5220 (gateway envoy 1.29->1.30 / HTTP-2) while the pool revert is evaluated; if latency does not recover within minutes of raising db.pool.max_size, then roll back dep-5220.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5220 precedes onset by ~2h with no intervening event and its known precedent (HIST-116) manifests as upstream resets, a signature absent from today's logs which are pool-acquisition timeouts. Keeping the gateway rollback in reserve avoids a second unnecessary change during mitigation.

recommended_actions.action: Verify mitigation on the exact signals: confirm portfolio-service db_pool_in_use falls back toward ~12 and stops pinning at 5, HikariPool 'Connection is not available ... total=5' errors cease, and api-gateway p99 and the 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings' 504 count return to baseline.
recommended_actions.rationale: These are the verified saturated-pool and upstream-timeout signals that established the causal chain; their reversal confirms the fix rather than merely coinciding with it.

recommended_actions.action: Query database-layer telemetry for ledger-db (and redis-cache) over 09:45-11:59Z — query latency, lock waits, connection/refused counts — to confirm the DB itself was not degraded, distinguishing H1 (too-few-slots) from H3 (shared-store fault) and from a slow-query/leaked-connection mechanism.
recommended_actions.rationale: No DB/cache component telemetry was queried, so the mechanism filling the pool and any shared-store contribution remains unverified; this is the discriminating check for the residual alternatives.

recommended_actions.action: Add guardrails to the cost-optimisation profile application: require minimum pool sizes validated against observed concurrency (baseline was ~12 in-use against max 50) and block automated profile changes to datasource pool size without a canary or validation step.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 50->5 step was applied by infra-automation with no recorded canary/percentage or sizing rationale; HIST-115's resolution was 'Reverted config; added validation', the same remedy this recurrence needs.

recommended_actions.action: Improve pool-saturation observability: alert on db_pool_in_use approaching max and on HikariPool acquisition-timeout errors per service, and pull DB-layer metrics as standard context for gateway latency incidents.
recommended_actions.rationale: The pool pegged at 5 for 2+ hours with only log-level visibility and no DB telemetry, which slowed attribution between the config cause and the shared-store alternative.

data_gaps: No DB/cache component telemetry was queried (no DB-layer metrics for ledger-db or redis-cache), so whether the underlying datastore is slow/unresponsive versus the pool being capped at too few slots cannot be fully separated from logs alone.

Dependency graph provides topology only, without telemetry values, so which node on the portfolio path degraded first — portfolio-service's pool versus a shared component — is not directly observable.

The rollout percentage/scope of the HTTP/2 enablement is not recorded (no canary or percentage field), so it cannot be confirmed whether HTTP/2 applied to 100% or a subset of portfolio traffic at 08:00Z.

No deployment/config history exists for the earlier 2026-03-09 window, so a normal-day change-volume baseline cannot be established and slow-burn or un-recorded changes before 03-09 cannot be excluded.
No rollback of cfg-2207 or dep-5220 appears in the window, so the mitigation/rollback effect (whether raising pool size restores latency) has not been observed; incident appears ongoing at 11:59Z.

The reported gateway 'HTTP/2 to upstreams' upgrade had no deploy/version/restart log or restart metric examined, so the correlation between the upgrade and onset cannot be directly confirmed or refuted from gateway-side evidence.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Reverting cfg-2207 (restoring db.pool.max_size to 50) fails to restore latency while rolling back dep-5220 resolves it — that would move the conclusion to H2 (gateway HTTP/2 change).

Evidence that the HikariPool was saturated by long-held or leaked connections (slow ledger-db queries, lock waits, or a connection leak) rather than by the 50->5 cap — e.g. DB-level latency/lock telemetry showing degradation beginning at ~09:45Z independent of the config step — would support H3 and shift the effective root cause to the datastore.
Direct evidence of a shared ledger-db or redis-cache fault (failover, refused connections, or latency spike) coincident with 09:52-09:55Z would favor H3 over H1.
Evidence of an actual portfolio traffic/concurrency surge around 09:50Z (roughly 4x+ over the ~12-connection baseline) would favor H4 over H1.
Discovery that the pool saturation or its onset predates cfg-2207 (e.g. pool pegging observable before 09:52Z) would break the temporal chain to H1.
Evidence that cfg-2207 was applied to a canary/subset only, or that its actual applied value on the live instances differs from 5, would weaken the causal link to the observed pin at 5.0.
